consensus_summary: Jacob primarily symbolizes the nation/covenant people of Israel (via renaming) and secondarily the individual supplanter transformed by grace into an overcomer, the elect, or the fleshly nature contrasted with Israel.
book_summary: The crooked, supplanting human heart that God transforms.
consensus_core_identification: Israel/covenant people or the (transformed) supplanting natural person/nature
book_core_identification: the crooked/supplanting human heart that God transforms
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the symbol strictly to the inner heart (linked to Jer 17:9) and omits the primary consensus corporate/national Israel sense and broader person-level cases, while retaining only the supplanter-transformation motif.
material_contradiction: None; the heart is the locus of the supplanting nature and transformation already present in consensus alternatives treating Jacob as fleshly/natural man.
rationale: Consensus cores center on Israel as people or the whole supplanter-turned-overcomer; the book preserves that transformation/supplanter category as its entire identification but narrows the referent to the human heart specifically. This changes extension and precision (heart cases are a subset of person/nature cases) without replacing the central category or contradicting listed alternatives that already treat Jacob as fleshly nature. Extra consensus detail on election, typology, or nation does not create artificial divergence once reduced to minimum cores.
strongest_objection: Settled consensus primary is corporate Israel (renaming + prophetic interchange), not the heart; Jer 17:9 has no direct Jacob link and the printed verses alone do not establish the transformation claim.
